current_date: August 2024 (document cover: 'Mansfield District Council Local Validation Checklist - Adopted August 2024'; file Final_validation_list_Aug_2024.docx)
current_evidence: The council's 'Apply for planning permission' page links to file 3149 as 'scheme of validation for planning applications document'. Searches found only older versions (file 679, file 733, 'local validation checklist 2022' file 3012 and the June 2022 committee version), so 3149 is the latest. The user-downloaded file (Final_validation_list_Aug_2024.docx) is the 'Local Validation Checklist, Adopted August 2024', which matches Grokbot's link and date.

issues.detail: Householder is set to '(none)' (national requirements only). Para 4.1 says householder schemes need more than the national items when the property is a listed building, in a conservation area, covered by a TPO or in a flood zone. Several Table Two triggers reach householder schemes: Heritage Statement (2.14, any proposal that may affect designated heritage assets or their setting), Tree survey/AIA (2.31, development that may affect a TPO tree), FRA (2.10, all new built development in Flood Zones 2 and 3), bat survey (2.7, demolition or significant alterations to the roof or loft space) and Coal Mining Risk Assessment (2.5, sites in the Coal Authority Development High Risk Area).
issues.evidence: 4.1 'This is unless your application relates to property that is Listed Building, in a Conservation Area, covered by a Tree Preservation Order, or within a Flood Zone.'

issues.detail: Every local requirement is filed only under Full planning, and most are flagged 'INFERRED'. Outline and Reserved matters are '(none)'. Table Three has separate columns for outline applications (minor and major residential, commercial, other major) and for reserved matters, and many Table Two triggers say 'All Major Developments', which covers outline majors. Examples are Air Quality (2.2), Building for a Healthy Life (2.4), Heads of Terms (2.12), Archaeology (2.14), LVIA (2.16), Planning Statement (2.20), Renewable Energy (2.21) and Secured by Design (2.24). Tree survey/AIA is filed only under Works to trees, although 2.31 also applies to 'All major development schemes' and to any development that may affect a TPO tree.
issues.evidence: Table Three columns 'Outline Application - Major Residential (+ 0.5ha) ... Outline Application - Other Major, Reserved Matters'; 2.31 'All major development schemes.'

issues.detail: Listed building consent and Demolition in conservation area are '(none)'. The document applies the Heritage Statement (2.14) to proposals affecting designated heritage assets, including conservation areas. It applies the Structural Survey (2.28) to the demolition, partial demolition or conversion of a listed building. Table Three has 'Listed Building Consent' and 'Development in a Conservation Area' columns.
issues.evidence: 2.28 'The demolition, or partial demolition of a Listed building(s), or The conversion of a Listed building.'

issues.detail: The Affordable Housing Statement (2.1) is missing. Trigger: planning applications for 10 or more dwellings or sites of 0.5 hectares or more. The statement must show compliance with Policy H4 parts 4 and 5.
issues.evidence: 2.1 'Planning applications for sites of 10 or more dwellings or where the site area is 0.5 hectares or more.'

issues.detail: The Heritage Statement (2.14) is missing. Grokbot captured only the archaeology half of 2.14. Trigger: all development proposals that will or may affect designated heritage assets or their setting, including conservation areas, locally listed buildings, non-designated assets and scheduled ancient monuments.
issues.evidence: 2.14 'All development proposals which will/may impact designated Heritage Assets and/or their settings (including conservation areas, locally listed buildings. Non designated assets and Scheduled Ancient Monuments).'

issues.detail: The Planning Statement including Statement of Community Involvement (2.20) is missing. Triggers: all major developments; alternative uses on allocated employment sites (E3); loss of open space (IN3); development on allotment land (IN5); leisure and visitor facilities (RT11); loss of existing facilities such as pubs, churches or community centres (IN7); and development affecting playing field land, with the Sport England Appendix A checklist.
issues.evidence: 2.20 'Planning Statement including Statement of Community Involvement - All Major Developments. ... Development affecting playing field land.'

issues.detail: Site Waste Management (2.26) is missing. Trigger: all applications for residential or commercial development, including changes of use, that will affect the generation of waste. A plan of bin storage locations, bin sizes and the design and materials of any bin enclosure is required.
issues.evidence: 2.26 'All applications for residential or commercial development (including changes of use) that will have an impact on the generation of waste.'

issues.detail: The Building for a Healthy Life Assessment (2.4) is missing. Trigger: all major developments (Policies P1 and P2).
issues.evidence: 2.4 'Building for a Healthy Life Assessment | All Major Developments'

issues.detail: The local Biodiversity Net Gain Statement (2.3) is missing. Trigger: all applications not exempt from BNG. It requires a post-development metric, the mitigation hierarchy steps, the onsite/offsite/credits strategy and any Significant On-Site Enhancements. Grokbot's single BNG row quotes only the national major-development metric (1.13). The small sites metric option for minor developments (1.14) is not reflected either.
issues.evidence: 2.3 'Biodiversity Net Gain Statement | All applications not exempt from biodiversity net gain.'
issues.grok_comment: The workbook does have a 'Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG) information / metric' row, but it is drawn from 1.13 'Biodiversity Net Gain Metric (Major developments)'; the separate local 2.3 BNG Statement ('All applications not exempt') is not captured.
issues.claude_response: Partly accepted. The BNG metric row exists for majors; the separate local BNG Statement for all non-exempt applications is still missing.

issues.detail: The Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan (2.11) is missing. Trigger: applications that propose Significant On-Site Enhancements for Biodiversity Net Gain. A draft HMMP is required.
issues.evidence: 2.11 'Applications where Significant On-Site Enhancements for Biodiversity Net Gain are proposed.'

issues.detail: The Minerals Statement (2.18) is missing. Trigger: major applications in Mineral Safeguarding and Consultation Areas in the Nottinghamshire Minerals Local Plan (Policy NE4).
issues.evidence: 2.18 'Major Applications in Mineral Safeguarding and Consultation Areas as set out in the Nottinghamshire Minerals Local Plan'

issues.detail: The Noise Impact Assessment (2.19) is missing. Triggers: development that would generate significant noise or vibration near residential or commercial properties, or a noise-sensitive use near a known noise source. The assessment must be prepared by a suitably qualified acoustician.
issues.evidence: 2.19 'Instances where the development would generate significant levels of noise or vibration ... or it proposes a noise sensitive use in proximity to a known noise source.'

issues.detail: The Renewable Energy Statement (2.21) is missing. Trigger: major applications and all applications for renewable energy production (Policy P5).
issues.evidence: 2.21 'Major applications and all applications for renewable energy production.'

issues.detail: The Public Right of Way Statement and Plan (2.22) is missing. Triggers: a public right of way within the application boundary, along the outside edge of the site, or nearby and likely to see more use as a result of the development.
issues.evidence: 2.22 'All applications where a Right of Way (RoW) exists: within the application boundary, OR alongside the outside edge of the development OR where a RoW in the close vicinity is likely to receive increased use'

issues.detail: The Slope Stability Assessment (2.27) is missing. Trigger: all minor and major residential applications next to a substantial slope, e.g. more than 2m. It is independently assessed at the applicant's cost.
issues.evidence: 2.27 'All minor and major residential applications located adjacent to a substantial slope e.g. more than 2m'

issues.detail: The Town Centre Design Code compliance checklist (2.29) is missing. Trigger: all major developments in Mansfield Town Centre, as defined in the Mansfield Town Centre Design Code (November 2023). The council's checklist template must be completed.
issues.evidence: 2.29 'All Major Developments in Mansfield Town Centre (as defined in the adopted Mansfield Town Centre Design Code November 2023)'

issues.detail: Two requirements appear only as run-on tab_items fragments and have no app_type_rows. They are the Secured by Design Assessment (2.24, all major applications) and the School Site Suitability Checklist (2.23, residential or mixed use schemes that include a new primary or secondary school site). The earlier claim that the HIA had no app_type_row is wrong: it is filed under Full planning, although with the wrong trigger (see below).
issues.evidence: 2.24 'Secured by Design Assessment | All Major Applications.'; 2.23 'Any planning application for a residential or mixed use development that includes a site for a new primary or secondary school'

issues.detail: The Health Impact Assessment trigger quotes the mitigation sentence, not the thresholds. Actual triggers: (A) residential development of 50 or more dwellings; (B) non-residential development of 5,000 sq m or more; (C) other development likely to have a significant impact on health and wellbeing.
issues.evidence: 2.13 'A. residential development of 50 dwellings or more; B. non-residential developments of 5,000 square metres or more'

issues.detail: The Planning Obligations / S106 Heads of Terms trigger quotes the CCG primary healthcare contribution on 'major proposals (above 15 dwellings)', which is an advisory note. The actual triggers are all major developments and sites above 0.5 hectares (affordable housing). The submission is a letter agreeing the heads of terms, up-to-date title deeds and the solicitor's contact details.
issues.evidence: 2.12 'All Major Developments. Sites above 0.5 hectares (Affordable Housing).'

issues.detail: The three flood rows omit the local thresholds. The FRA row says only 'where one is required under the NPPF'. The Drainage row is the fragment 'systems including Sustainable Drainage (SuDS).' The Sequential/Exception Test row omits that it applies in Flood Zones 2 and 3. Actual 2.10 triggers: all major developments; Flood Zone 1 sites of 1 ha or more, sites under 1 ha with critical drainage problems, or sites under 1 ha changing to a more vulnerable use; and all new built development in Flood Zones 2 and 3.
issues.evidence: 2.10 'All Major Developments; All developments in Floodzone 1 when: - The site is 1 hectare or greater ... All new built development within Flood Zones 2 and 3.'

issues.detail: The Ecology trigger is the fragment 'accompanied by a bat survey report.' The HRA/SPA row and tab_item join the 400m SPA trigger to the EcIA definition from another column. Actual 2.7 triggers: an EcIA for sites on or next to statutory or non-statutory nature conservation sites, sites with natural habitats, or where protected species could be nearby; a bat survey for demolition, significant roof or loft alterations, agricultural building conversions, or large trees to be removed or significantly pruned; and a risk-based assessment within 400m of the possible potential Sherwood Forest SPA.
issues.evidence: 2.7 'Where a proposal involves the demolition of a structure or significant alterations to the roof and/or loft space, or the conversion of an agricultural building, then the application must be accompanied by a bat survey report.'

issues.detail: The Archaeological Assessment trigger quotes mitigation wording ('Where necessary ... usually before commencement'), not when it applies. Actual triggers: applications for major development, and development on or next to a heritage asset of archaeological interest.
issues.evidence: 2.14 'Applications for major development; Applications for development known to be on or adjacent to a heritage asset of archaeological interest'

issues.detail: The Structural Survey trigger is taken from the Heritage Statement text ('may also be required in support of any demolition works'). The actual 2.28 triggers are the demolition, partial demolition or conversion of a listed building, and the conversion of agricultural buildings.
issues.evidence: 2.28 'The demolition, or partial demolition of a Listed building(s), or The conversion of a Listed building. Conversion of Agricultural Buildings.'

issues.detail: The External Lighting Scheme trigger quotes the ecological constraints sentence and does not say when a scheme is needed. Actual trigger: floodlighting or external lighting next to residential properties, outside the urban boundary, in or next to a conservation area, on or next to a listed building, or in the town centres.
issues.evidence: 2.9 'If floodlighting or external lighting is proposed on a site adjacent to residential properties, outside the urban boundary, adjacent or within a Conservation Area or adjacent/on a Listed Building and buildings within the town centres.'

issues.detail: The Contaminated Land trigger is the fragment 'with possible land contamination should include: Site Investigation/Detailed Investigation'. Actual triggers: new development on former petrol filling stations, landfill or industrial sites; development with a vulnerable end user such as housing; and sites with known contamination on or around them. At minimum, a desk study and site walkover report are required.
issues.evidence: 2.15 'New developments on former petrol filling stations, former landfill sites and former industrial sites. Development with a vulnerable end user (e.g. residential development).'

issues.detail: The 'Design Code / Masterplan / Parameter plans' row merges two separate requirements, and its trigger is cut off at the start ('or more) a masterplan...'). This drops the threshold. The Masterplan (2.17) applies to sites of 5ha or more or 150 dwellings or more. The Design Code (2.6) applies to large-scale major applications, and its trigger is not captured.
issues.evidence: 2.17 'Sites of 5ha or more or 150 dwellings or more.'; 2.6 'Design Code | Large Scale Major Application.'

issues.detail: The retail row gives no threshold or location. Sequential test: main town centre uses that are neither in an existing centre nor in line with the local plan. Retail impact: retail and leisure schemes over 500 sq m (net) in edge-of-centre or out-of-centre locations that are not allocated. The impact assessment is checked by a third party at the applicant's expense.
issues.evidence: 2.25 'Retail and leisure developments over 500 sqm (net) which are proposed in edge of centre and out of centre locations and which are not allocated in the Local Plan.'

issues.detail: The 'Cycle parking details' trigger is the fragment 'spaces and cycle storage areas in new developments.' The requirement (2.33) covers vehicle parking, cycle storage, EV charging points, loading and servicing on a scaled plan. It applies to proposals for new dwellings and to new or changed employment premises.
issues.evidence: 2.33 'Vehicle Parking, Cycle Storage and Electric Charging Points | Proposals for new dwellings and/or new or changes to employment premises.'

issues.detail: The Tree survey/AIA trigger gives only the first of three triggers (felling a protected tree) and has a stray 'NPPF 2.31' prefix. It omits development that may affect a TPO tree and all major development schemes.
issues.evidence: 2.31 'Where a development proposal may have an impact on a TPO tree. All major development schemes.'

issues.detail: The 'Open space / play space assessment' row is the Sport England playing-fields sentence from the Planning Statement (2.20), and its trigger starts mid-sentence. The document has no separate open space or play space assessment. The trigger is development affecting playing field land, with the Appendix A Sport England checklist.
issues.evidence: 2.20 'Sport England recommends that planning applications affecting playing fields should provide specific information in line with the appendix in Appendix A'

issues.detail: The Viability Assessment trigger quotes the 'what is required' text. The actual trigger is schemes that do not meet all policy requirements, such as affordable housing or education, because doing so would make them unviable.
issues.evidence: 2.32 'Where schemes are not proposing to meet all policy requirements, such as affordable housing, education etc.'

issues.detail: The LVIA trigger covers major developments but omits the second trigger: developments in or next to Landscape Policy Zones that are likely to have a significant adverse impact.
issues.evidence: 2.16 'All major developments those developments in and adjacent to Landscape Policy Zones likely to have a significant adverse impact.'

issues.detail: The Environmental Statement trigger quotes the general statement about the EIA Regulations. The document's trigger is Schedule 1 development, or Schedule 2 development likely to have significant effects. A screening opinion should be requested for all applications over 0.5ha.
issues.evidence: 2.8 'The developer should request a 'screening opinion' (all applications over 0.5ha) from the local planning authority'

issues.detail: Several triggers carry text from the neighbouring table cells or are cut off. Air Quality starts '65 2.2' and BNG starts 'development. 1.13'. Coal Mining starts 'P2 2.5' and stops at 'geological inform'. Transport starts 'Policies P1 and S4 2.30', but P1 and S4 belong to 2.29 and the transport policies are IN9 and IN10. The tab_items run rows together, as in 'NPPF Para 104 Policies IN2 and IN8 2.23 ...' and '... NPPF Para 99 2.24 Secured by Design Assessment All Major Applications.'
issues.evidence: 2.30 policy column 'Policies IN9 and IN10'; app_type_rows trigger_excerpt values

issues.detail: 'Advertisement drawings / illumination details' is not an advertisement requirement. Its text ('a polar luminance diagram ... shall be submitted') comes from the External Lighting Scheme (2.9), so it duplicates the lighting row under the wrong name. The document has no advertisement-specific local requirement, so the earlier suggestion to move this row to Advertisement consent was wrong.
issues.evidence: 2.9 External Lighting Scheme 'Hours of operation and details of lighting spill (to include a polar luminance diagram based on vertical luminance at the nearest sensitive premises)'

issues.detail: 'Highways / access details (visibility splays)' is not a local requirement. Its trigger comes from the national Site Location Plan guidance (1.4) on what land the red line should include.
issues.evidence: 1.4 Site Location Plan 'land required for access to the site from a public highway, visibility splays, landscaping, car parking and open areas around buildings.'

issues.detail: 'Pre-application advice / engagement details' is not a validation requirement. It is a sentence from the Design Code entry (2.6) about how a design code should be prepared.
issues.evidence: 2.6 'This shall be devised through pre-application engagement with the council and potentially with an external design review.'

issues.detail: Some tab_items are process text or fragments, not requirements. They are the Planning Portal hard-copy forms sentence, the Table One heading run into the application form text, and drawing-standard lines run together across items 1.7 to 1.11. One of those carries a stray 'Fire safety and high-rise residential buildings (from 1 August 2021) - GOV.UK (' prefix.
issues.evidence: 5.1 'Should you wish to submit hard copies, application forms can be obtained directly from the Planning Portal.'

summary: Grokbot's link and list date are correct: the document is Mansfield's Local Validation Checklist, 'Adopted August 2024'. The contents extraction is poor. Of the 33 local requirements in Table Two, 13 are missing entirely, including the Affordable Housing Statement, Heritage Statement, Planning Statement, Site Waste Management and Building for a Healthy Life, and two more appear only as tab_item fragments. Most captured rows quote mid-paragraph or wrong-requirement text instead of the 'When is this required?' column. Everything is filed under Full planning, while Householder, Outline, Reserved matters and Listed building consent are wrongly shown as having no local requirements.
